Read IN FULL: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev/646bc8ac-afb6-41b4-8d24-dcbaf28144cd/scratchpad/turns_chunk05.txt

This file contains every user turn Marcel Navarro typed across ~58 Claude Code sessions while working as FED Lead on the Zimmermann PWA Kit (a Salesforce PWA Kit / React / Chakra codebase). Sessions are separated by `====` lines with a `### [tag] [date] Title — N user turns` header. Turns are marked `--- turn N ---`.

READ THE WHOLE FILE. It is large (~450,000 tokens), so read it in sequential slices using Read with offset/limit. Maintain a running findings list as you go and DISCARD raw text after each slice — never try to hold the whole file in context.

We are designing personal workflow skills for Marcel. The transcripts are the evidence for WHY those skills are needed. Extract these six things:

**1. RECURRING CORRECTIONS — the highest priority.**
Places where Marcel had to re-state an established way of working that had been ignored or got wrong. He has said he had to "stress again and again" the set approach. Find those. For each, give: verbatim quote (trimmed to the relevant sentences), the session title, turn number, and tag it with the area:
`overriding` | `tokens` | `components` | `atomic-design` (atoms/molecules/organisms) | `css-structure` | `css-strategy` | `tests` | `stories` | `a11y` | `typescript` | `contentful` | `scope` | `git/branching` | `other`
Count how many DISTINCT times each area comes up. That count is the single most important output.

**2. DESIGN CONFORMANCE.**
Where he had to check or re-check that a build matched the Figma design — variants, states, tokens, viewports, spacing. Quote the checks he actually performs and what he looks for.

**3. FRUSTRATION / RE-WORK SIGNALS.**
Turns containing corrections: "again", "I said", "no —", "that's not", "you missed", "why did you", "revert", "you were supposed to", "as I mentioned". These mark where the workflow broke down. Quote and categorise.

**4. WHAT WORKED.**
Successes. Especially any use of a closed-loop / multi-agent / orchestrator-builder-tester-scorer workflow. Quote how he set it up and what he said about the result. Also note any prompt pattern he reused because it worked.

**5. HIS PROMPT FORMULAS.**
Recurring phrasings and structures he types — the shape of his asks. We want to encode his voice and method into skills, so capture the actual language, not a paraphrase.

**6. REVIEW-MODE BEHAVIOUR.**
He is also senior dev / reviewer. Where he reviews others' PRs or code, capture: what he checks, in what order, what he rejects, and how he phrases feedback.

OUTPUT: a structured report with these six sections. Lead section 1 with a frequency table of areas. Use verbatim quotes throughout — quotes are the deliverable, not summaries. Be concrete. If a section has nothing, say so explicitly.

## 6. REVIEW-MODE BEHAVIOUR

### A. Reviewing another dev's PR — the fixed order (PR #68, *New session*)

1. **Story before code.** > "we're working on PR #68 but **before we focus into the code, let's look into the JIRA ticket / user story first** so we can take note of the user story: it's requirements, ACs, description, separation of concerns, scope, etc. in-depth and full-on - what we obtain, we store on a temporary local .MD in /Desktop for ease of access" (t2)
2. **Run the tooling, then verdict.** > "let's run code-review and code-quality, test the changes, and then **we either approve or request changes**" (t3)
3. **House-style conformance is the acceptance bar.** > "fully aligned with the set and established approach as to how we build code (overriding, tokens, components, file structuring, css structuring, etc.)" (t3)
4. **Right-size the machinery.** > "but scaled appropriately to the need, nothing too crazy/too much and most definitely no overthinking" (t4)
5. **Validate the feedback before delivering it.** > "before we post these comments, let's run them and see their feasibility while also testing them, run it" (t8)
6. **Decide the delivery mechanics.** > "how do we comment? as one of in-line to the codes in question?" (t9) / "any non in-line comments like general comments?" (t11)
7. **Tone rule.** > "use natural language as much as possible **without sacrifing the technical aspect of the review**" (t10)
8. **Filter.** > "anything not 'code-focused' we take out of the comments" (t12)
9. **Ship.** > "go for commenting the review on the PR in github" (t13)

**What he rejects:** anything not code-focused; unverified findings; over-scaled process.

### B. Reviewing a branch diff — the fixed order (*Design2Dev*)

> 1. "aside from the changes specific to this branch - **is this branch up to date with the latest from develop?** and then walk me through the diff" (t2)
> 2. State the intended scope explicitly, then judge the diff against it (t2)
> 3. "**what are diffs that fall outside of this main scope, list them down**, and then technicalities aside… **which of these items… genuinely provide value** to the goal" (t3)
> 4. **Reject rule-lawyered rejections** — "I want to know if these flags are out of complete and utter necessity or if they are just being flagged out of technicalities" (t4)
